title: ASD_AN02987_ba41-42-22_8.6
extract_protocol_ch1: Approximately 100mg of tissue across the cortical region of interest was isolated from each sample for up to two RNA extractions using the miRNeasy kit (Qiagen). The best RNA extraction based on RIN was used for RNA-seq.
extract_protocol_ch1.1: Ribosomal RNA was depleted from 2ug total RNA with the Ribo-Zero Gold kit (Epicentre). Remaining RNA was then size selected with AMPure XP beads (Beckman Coulter) and resuspended in 8.5 ul of Illumina resuspension buffer and an additional 8.5 ul of 2x EPF buffer. Subsequent steps followed the Illumina TruSeq protocol (starting at page 84 of the sample prep v2 guide, no changes). After this protocol was followed, libraries were quantified with the Quant-iT PicoGreen assay (Life Technologies) and validated on an Agilent 2200 TapeStation system. Libraries were pooled to multiplex 24 samples per lane using Illumina barcodes, and each pool was sequenced six times on a HiSeq2000/2500 instrument using high output mode with standard chemistry and protocols for 50bp paired end reads. Most libraries were sequenced across two sequencing cores at UCLA. Read quality was similar across both core facilities, and reads across six lanes for each sample were pooled after demultiplexing (with Casava v1.8) for downstream analysis.
data_processing: Aligned to the Human reference genome assembly GRCh37.73 using Tophat2 {v2.0.9, Trapnell:2012gg} as follows:  tophat -o outputfolder -g 10 -p 8 -r 99 --no-novel-juncs -G GRCh37.73.gtf hg19bowtieindex pairedread1.fastq pairedread2.fastq  Aligned reads were sorted and reads mapped to different chromosomes were removed from the BAM file using samtools v0.1.19.
data_processing.1: Quantification of gene expression levels with HTSeq (v.0.6.1) with a union exon model as follows:  python -m HTSeq.scripts.count --stranded=no --mode=union --type=exon --quiet inputfile.sam --GTF GRCh37.73.gtf >> outputfolder
data_processing.2: Calculated FPKM values from count level data as follows: datFPM <- sweep(log2(datExpr + 1), 2, log2(apply(datExpr,2,sum)/10^6))  keep <- apply(datFPM>1,1,sum)>(0.80*ncol(datFPM)) ## Keep those with > 1 FPM in 80% of samples                                         datExpr <- datFPM[keep,]. Adjusted expression values were calculated by running the following linear model: lm.out <- lm(thisExpr ~ diagnosis + age + sex + RIN + brainbank + seqStatPC1 + seqStatPC2); where seqStatPC1 and seqStatPC2 are calculated from the first two principal components from the 15 sequencing quality metrics. Followed by: thisExpr.reg <- coef[1] + coef[2]*regvars[,""diagnosis""] + lm.out$residuals; where coef[1] and coef[2] are the intercept and the coefficient corresponding to diagnosis, respectively.
data_processing.4: Supplementary_files_format_and_content: Count-level data generated by HTSeq; adjusted FPKM values generated in R as described in the data processing step

Remaining RNA was then size selected with AMPure XP beads (Beckman Coulter) and resuspended in 8.5 ul of Illumina resuspension buffer and an additional 8.5 ul of 2x EPF buffer. Subsequent steps followed the Illumina TruSeq protocol (starting at page 84 of the sample prep v2 guide, no changes). After this protocol was followed, libraries were quantified with the Quant-iT PicoGreen assay (Life Technologies) and validated on an Agilent 2200 TapeStation system. Libraries were pooled to multiplex 24 samples per lane using Illumina barcodes, and each pool was sequenced six times on a HiSeq2000/2500 instrument using high output mode with standard chemistry and protocols for 50bp paired end reads. Most libraries were sequenced across two sequencing cores at UCLA. Read quality was similar across both core facilities, and reads across six lanes for each sample were pooled after demultiplexing (with Casava v1.8) for downstream analysis.
data_processing: Aligned to the Human reference genome assembly GRCh37.73 using Tophat2 {v2.0.9, Trapnell:2012gg} as follows:  tophat -o outputfolder -g 10 -p 8 -r 99 --no-novel-juncs -G GRCh37.73.gtf hg19bowtieindex pairedread1.fastq pairedread2.fastq  Aligned reads were sorted and reads mapped to different chromosomes were removed from the BAM file using samtools v0.1.19.
data_processing.1: Quantification of gene expression levels with HTSeq (v.0.6.1) with a union exon model as follows:  python -m HTSeq.scripts.count --stranded=no --mode=union --type=exon --quiet inputfile.sam --GTF GRCh37.73.gtf >> outputfolder
data_processing.2: Calculated FPKM values from count level data as follows: datFPM <- sweep(log2(datExpr + 1), 2, log2(apply(datExpr,2,sum)/10^6))  keep <- apply(datFPM>1,1,sum)>(0.80*ncol(datFPM)) ## Keep those with > 1 FPM in 80% of samples                                         datExpr <- datFPM[keep,]. Adjusted expression values were calculated by running the following linear model: lm.out <- lm(thisExpr ~ diagnosis + age + sex + RIN + brainbank + seqStatPC1 + seqStatPC2); where seqStatPC1 and seqStatPC2 are calculated from the first two principal components from the 15 sequencing quality metrics. Followed by: thisExpr.reg <- coef[1] + coef[2]*regvars[,""diagnosis""] + lm.out$residuals; where coef[1] and coef[2] are the intercept and the coefficient corresponding to diagnosis, respectively.
data_processing.4: Supplementary_files_format_and_content: Count-level data generated by HTSeq; adjusted FPKM values generated in R as described in the data processing step
